step1_summary.Chief complaint: Aching all over with tiredness and feeling run down for about six weeks.
Symptoms: Onset: Around late January to early February (about six weeks ago), a couple of weeks after returning from a holiday in the USA.
Severity: Moderate, causing decreased energy and reduced exercise tolerance.
Aggravating/alleviating factors: No clear aggravating or relieving factors; reduced physical activity noted.

Additional symptoms: Transient rash on back of calf (noticed late February, lasted a couple of weeks, mild/no itching), some aching in shoulders, back, hips, knees without swelling; mild sore throat and possible low-grade fever around rash onset; no weight change, no GI or urinary symptoms, no respiratory symptoms, no neurological symptoms, no joint swelling.
step1_summary.Medications/allergies: Uses asthma preventative inhaler regularly, takes OTC antihistamines occasionally, no new medications mentioned.
step1_summary.Family/social history: Lives with wife, works in health technology, occasional alcohol use, no smoking.
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: No vital signs or physical exam details documented.
step1_summary.Labs/imaging: None done yet, blood tests planned including infection screen (specifically Lyme disease).

V: Lyme disease: Endemic area exposure with history of rash (possibly erythema migrans), systemic symptoms of fatigue and arthralgia; rash on calf consistent with tick bite site.
Other vascular/inflammatory conditions less likely given no focal signs.
I: Post-infectious or persistent viral syndrome: Fatigue and generalized pains after potential viral illness leading to low-grade fever and sore throat.
Chronic infection other than Lyme is less likely without typical signs.
N: Chronic fatigue syndrome or paraneoplastic syndrome: Fatigue and aching over weeks could rarely be initial presentation of malignancy.
D: Vitamin D deficiency or other nutritional deficiency: Generalized aching and fatigue over weeks could be due to deficiencies.
No direct dietary history but decreased appetite noted.
I2: Medication side effect or intoxication unlikely given no new drugs reported.
Antihistamines or asthma inhalers typically do not cause these symptoms.
C: No congenital condition suggested by onset and symptoms.
A: Early autoimmune disease (e.g., inflammatory arthritis or connective tissue disease): Aching joints without swelling, rash, fatigue could precede overt signs.
No joint swelling or morning stiffness reported; rash transient and limited.
E: Hypothyroidism or other endocrine causes: Fatigue and generalized aches fit hypothyroidism; no mention of cold intolerance or weight changes though.
Diabetes less likely without polyuria or other symptoms.
